method: Each ticket's digest (every review, close-out and implementation comment from the first code review on, interleaved with every commit naming the ticket in either repo) read by one of ten in-session subagents of the frontier tier, one batch each, against the rubric below, fixed before reading; the Clarifications were added after the first four batches and applied to them by the author. Not second-read.
rubric:
# Consequence coding rubric (LIN-3156) — fixed before reading

You read one digest per ticket: every review, close-out and implementation comment from the ticket's
first code review onward (orchestrator/plan comments are listed by heading only), interleaved with every
commit that names the ticket in either repo (LinearViewer or simple-dispatcher). Each commit line gives
lines changed by file class: `prod` (LinearViewer lib/, routes/, public/, server.js; simple-dispatcher
top-level *.js/*.sh), `test`, `docs`, `other`. Commits marked `AFTER FIRST REVIEW` were authored after
the first review comment. Comment timestamps are UTC; commit timestamps carry their own offset.

## Unit of coding: a consequence

A *consequence* is one distinct finding raised by a code review (in a send-back, or as a ledger/gate
item under a conditional Approve) or one hold raised by a close-out, followed to what it changed. A
finding repeated in a later round is ONE consequence. Plan-review findings are out of scope. Findings a
review lists as "non-blocking / nit / note" count only if something was actually changed for them.

For each consequence record:

- `comment`: the index of the comment that raised it (`### comment N`).
- `leg`: `review` or `close-out`.
- `finding`: ≤ 20 words, what it said.
- `rules`: the rule(s) that directed the reviewer or close-out to raise it, primary first, from the ids in
  `data/survey/coding/rules.json` — or `general-judgement` when no specific rule directed it (a reviewer
  reading the code and seeing a bug is general judgement, NOT `requirements`, unless the finding is
  framed against the ticket's stated requirement/acceptance criterion). Hints:
  - "remove the code path and the test stays green" / a mutation run exposed a vacuous test → `mutation-check`
  - a second instance / sibling / missed caller of the same class → `class-check`
  - an item in the "What CI Did Not Prove" ledger that close-out or implementation then had to discharge → `ledger`
  - close-out refused to merge because a ledger item was undischarged → `ledger-discharge`
  - close-out refused to author an edit / merge conflict routed back → `trivial-edit-bound`
  - red CI / wrong commit / CI not re-run → `ci-green-exact-commit`
  - scope overrun / change beyond plan → `scope-drift`
  - missing e2e/integration test, or wrong test level → `test-adequacy`
  - screenshot / page load / visual check found it → `direct-verification`
  - reintroduces a previously fixed bug (git log check) → `regression-history`
  - security / error-handling / performance point → `quality-checklist`
  - monitor/rollback lane naming → `risk-lanes`
- `effect`: what it changed, judged from the commits and comments that followed it:
  - `prod` — a production-code change (a `prod`-line commit that the following comment ties to this finding)
  - `tests` — only tests, witnesses, pins, fixtures changed
  - `docs-wording` — only docs, PR/ticket/comment text, code comments, prompt wording in a docs file
  - `follow-up` — filed as a separate ticket; nothing changed here
  - `nothing` — dropped, accepted, argued away, or no change found
  Note: prompt/template text under `lib/` IS production code (it ships behaviour).
- `realFault`: true only if the finding identified a correctness fault that would have shipped wrong
  product behaviour had it merged (wrong output, crash/hang, broken UI, security/credential flaw, data
  loss, the change not taking effect). A missing test, a false claim in the record, style or scope is NOT
  a real fault even if it was fixed.
- `commits`: the short shas the finding caused (empty if none).
- `rounds`: the extra legs it caused: count each additional implementation beat + re-review (or
  close-out re-run) that this finding was a reason for; 0 if it was handled without another leg. If one
  round addressed several findings, give the round to each (we note the double count).
- `confidence`: high / medium / low.

Also record per ticket `unattributed`: post-review commits you cannot tie to any finding (rebases,
conflict resolutions, CI fixes, unrelated) as `{ sha, why }` (≤ 10 words), and `note` (≤ 25 words) if the
ticket is unusual (e.g. a parent whose code landed under children).

A ticket can have zero consequences (e.g. commits after the first review were only a rebase).

## Clarifications (added after the first four batches, applied to them afterwards)

- A change only under `scripts/`, `.github/`, `package*.json` or other dev tooling is effect `tooling`.
- A production change to mechanism code that has no production caller yet is still `prod`; `realFault`
  stays false unless the fault would have shipped once the code was live in this same ticket.
- Wording fixes in production prompt/instruction text under `lib/` are `prod`, `realFault` false.
- Ledger items the review itself marks outside the ticket or not owed, and that nothing acted on, are
  not consequences. An item handed to an existing ticket with a recorded note is `follow-up` (give that
  ticket as `followUp`); with no note it is `nothing`.
- If the real code review is in a comment the digest labels differently, code it anyway and say so in `note`.
